examples.ask: What do I use for a confirmation before deleting?

args.need: a modal to confirm deleting a project

examples.response:
Use:
- Dialog: Modal dialog.
  import { Dialog } from "@dsw/ui";

Call get_component for props and examples before using one.

args.need: a tooltip on an icon button

examples.response:
Not in @dsw/ui yet: Tooltip. Meanwhile: visible helper text (Text or a field's `description`), which also works on touch. Don't hand-build one; tell the user it's a gap for the design-system team.

Closest components:
- Button: Triggers an action.
  import { Button } from "@dsw/ui";

Call get_component for props and examples before using one.

# Badge

import { Badge } from "@dsw/ui";

A short, non-interactive status label. For a message, use Alert; for
something clickable, a Button or Link. Keep the text self-explanatory,
since the colour isn't announced.

## Props
- `children: ReactNode` — A word or two: "Active", "Admin", "Beta".
- `tone?: "neutral" | "accent" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"` — Colour role. Defaults to "neutral". The text must say the status too: tone is a reinforcement.

examples.ask: Does the code I just wrote follow the rules?
examples.response:
3 finding(s):
- L1:1 [@dsw/no-primitive-tokens] Don't use primitive tokens directly: they don't follow the theme and aren't contrast-audited. Use @dsw/tokens/semantic.stylex, or the component's tokens in @dsw/tokens/components.stylex.
- L3:10 [@dsw/prefer-layout-primitives] This style is a hand-written Inline. Use <Inline gap="…"> from @dsw/ui: it wraps by default so rows reflow at 320px, and can stack on phones.
- L3:32 [@dsw/no-raw-style-values] gap: Hardcoded style value "16px" — use a token from @dsw/tokens (or add `// token-exempt: <reason>`).
    try: space.lg (exact) = 16px | space.md = 12px | space.sm = 8px

A deliberate one-off may stay with a "// token-exempt: <reason>" comment on the same or previous line.

Build a page, screen, view or form with the @dsw design system (@dsw/ui components and @dsw/tokens).
Move existing app UI onto the @dsw design system.
Review UI code in an app that uses @dsw/ui for design-system compliance and accessibility.

rules.description: Require design tokens instead of hardcoded values in StyleX styles

example.message: Hardcoded style value "#6a58ee" — use a token from @dsw/tokens (or add `// token-exempt: <reason>`).
Don't use primitive tokens directly: they don't follow the theme and aren't contrast-audited. Use @dsw/tokens/semantic.stylex, or the component's tokens in @dsw/tokens/components.stylex.

rules.description: Import token groups from their origin file, not the @dsw/tokens barrel

example.message: Import color from its origin file (e.g. @dsw/tokens/semantic.stylex), not @dsw/tokens: StyleX can't trace token groups through a re-export.

rules.description: Avoid inline style objects in JSX

example.message: Avoid inline style objects: they bypass tokens and conflict with stylex.props(). Use a @dsw/ui component or stylex.create() (with a style function for runtime values).

rules.description: Use @dsw/ui components instead of the native elements they replace

example.message: Use <Button> from @dsw/ui instead of <button>: press handling for mouse, touch and keyboard, a focus ring, a loading state and themed variants.

rules.description: Import components from @dsw/ui rather than React Aria directly

example.message: Import Button from @dsw/ui, not react-aria-components: the unstyled primitive skips the system's tokens, brands and accessibility defaults. If @dsw/ui has no equivalent, raise it with the design-system team rather than styling your own.

rules.description: Use Stack, Inline or Grid from @dsw/ui instead of hand-written layout styles

example.message: This style is a hand-written Inline. Use <Inline gap="…"> from @dsw/ui: it wraps by default so rows reflow at 320px, and can stack on phones.
